true_positives.matched_candidate:
Escape the source URL before interpolating it into HTML

The source URL is inserted into both a single-quoted attribute and link text without escaping. A URL on the permitted host with a fragment such as `#'onclick='alert(1)` can pass URI host validation and fetch the original article, but produces an injected `onclick` attribute in the imported attribution link. This link is appended after Readability processes the article and is rendered through the raw-HTML path. Build the link with an escaping HTML helper rather than string interpolation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB closing statement prevents rendering existing discussions

The opening conditional is closed with `end if` rather than `end`. This produces invalid Ruby in the compiled template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail instead of displaying the discussion. Change this to `<%- end %>` and exercise the endpoint with view rendering enabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle RSS items that do not contain an Atom content field

The poller unconditionally reads `i.content.scrub`, but valid RSS items commonly supply their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can have only a summary. For these feeds the content value is absent, causing the poll to fail before importing the item or any subsequent entries. Select the appropriate available body field and handle entries without a body explicitly; add coverage using actual RSS and Atom fixtures.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve the original thread creation date during Disqus imports

The previous topic creation passed `t[:created_at]` to `PostCreator`; the replacement passes only the title, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` creates the first post with the current time. Replies still retain their historical timestamps, so imported topics now appear newly created and have replies dated before their opening post. Carry the original creation timestamp through the new import path.

Raw HTML posts bypass sanitization and allow stored XSS

Returning `raw` unchanged bypasses the rendering pipeline's HTML sanitization. The RSS poller passes external HTML directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, and `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts or event handlers. Consequently, feed content such as an image with an `onerror` handler is stored as executable cooked HTML under the forum's origin. Subsequent edits to these posts also retain this bypass. Sanitize raw-HTML posts before storing or rendering their cooked content.

Resolve relative URLs without corrupting protocol-relative links

Treating every leading slash as a root-relative path rewrites `//cdn.example.com/image.png` into a path on the article host, breaking protocol-relative images and links. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.png` and `../other-page` remain unchanged and resolve against the Discourse page rather than the source article. Resolve both `href` and `src` against the full source URL with URI resolution instead of manually stripping slashes.

Revalidate redirect destinations when retrieving an embedded article

`TopicRetriever` checks only the host of the initial URL, while `open(url)` automatically follows redirects without applying that restriction. An allowed-host redirect to another host, including a loopback or private-network HTTP service, therefore makes the worker fetch an otherwise forbidden destination and potentially publish its response as a topic. Validate each redirect destination and reject private/internal addresses before making the request.

Office 365 explicitly accepts refresh responses without a new refresh token and merges the parsed data into the existing credentials. This new placeholder overwrites the valid saved refresh token, so the next refresh fails. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement; do not fabricate one in the shared parser.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Replace computed schema keys with actual token-field validation

`z.string().toString()` does not define a wildcard property: it produces the literal key `[object Object]`. Both computed keys resolve to that same key, so the optional unknown schema overwrites the numeric schema. Since Zod objects strip unknown properties by default, a sync response such as `{ access_token: "token", expires_in: 3600 }` loses its expiry and any refresh token. Zoom then computes a NaN expiry, and Office 365 cannot persist the refreshed expiry. Define and preserve the actual supported response fields.

Saving this result directly as `credential.key` replaces the credential with a validation-result wrapper. This also affects installations with syncing disabled: after the first successful refresh, subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse the stored credentials. true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delegate Salesforce refreshes when credential sharing is enabled

The new Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce instead of using the configured credential-sync endpoint. For externally managed credentials, Cal.com may only have an access token and no usable refresh token; this request then fails before the connection is constructed, even if the supplied access token is still valid. Route this refresh through the same delegation mechanism as the other integrations and use the returned token in the connection.

This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Adapt Webex validation to the delegated token response

The new helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token lifetime. A response following the delegated-refresh contract is always rejected as invalid, preventing Webex meeting operations after token expiry. Add a delegated-response adapter and preserve the necessary existing credential metadata.

Authenticate requests that retrieve external access tokens

The outbound request contains only a numeric user ID and app slug, with no secret, signature, or authorization header. An ordinary HTTP sync endpoint therefore has no application-level way to distinguish Cal.com from a caller requesting another user's token. A protected endpoint must reject these requests; accepting them without additional infrastructure exposes tokens to anyone who can reach it. Add an authenticated outbound protocol rather than requiring an unauthenticated token lookup.

Clear invalid status when replacing credentials through the webhook

The update path replaces only `key`. Integrations such as Google Calendar and Zoom mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authentication failures. Sending replacement credentials through this webhook returns success but leaves that invalid status intact, so an external reconnection does not restore a healthy installed credential. Reset the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials.

Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce service

The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce operations.

Make initial webhook credential creation atomic

The lookup and create are separate operations without serialization. Two concurrent deliveries for the same new user/app pair can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Later deliveries update only whichever row `findFirst` selects, leaving the other credential stale and potentially causing duplicate integration processing. Make this operation idempotent under concurrent webhook delivery.

Send Zoom's app slug rather than its integration directory name

The sync request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with `appId: "zoom"`, and the new webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent application using that same slug to store and retrieve credentials cannot resolve this refresh request. Pass `"zoom"` here to keep the inbound and outbound contracts consistent.

Because the failure is unchecked, the script still reports that the URL was updated, leaving webhook testing pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement approach or handle the sed variants explicitly and check the result.

This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache

The delete-cache success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper passes an optional caller callback rather than refetching that query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Consequently, deleting the cache can show a success toast while continuing to display the old cache timestamp and deletion action until the page is reloaded. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Resolve cache status for in-memory delegation credentials

Connected calendars can use in-memory delegation credentials, but this lookup assumes every displayed credential ID is a database credential ID. CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability explicitly handles in-memory credentials by querying userId and the cache key, since their cache is stored under a real credential ID. Looking up status solely using the displayed credential ID therefore returns no status for those delegated calendars even when availability is being served from cache. Since the dropdown hides all cache actions when cacheUpdatedAt is null, affected users cannot inspect or clear that cache. Resolve the user's backing cache records for delegated connections and support that same identity in the deletion flow.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script

ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore edits or creates an .env outside the repository, leaving the application's GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged despite printing success. Derive the repository path from BASH_SOURCE before locating .env.

Use the correct process type when killing unhealthy workers

These are not instances of multiprocessing.Process, so this check is false for production workers and process.kill() is never called. A worker declared hung therefore remains alive while its replacement starts flushing the same shards, potentially producing duplicates and updating the replacement's shared health/backpressure state.
